newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rescuers free 148 people from Russian tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers free 148 people from Russian tunnel.

text.p: Rescue teams using helicopters on Wednesday evacuated 148 people from a tunnel in the Caucasus mountains where they had been trapped for almost a week by avalanches, Russia's Emergencies Ministry said.

A ministry spokesman said about 60 people, mainly drivers, had opted to stay put because they did not want to abandon their vehicles in or near the tunnel, linking Russia's North Ossetia region and the breakaway Georgian province of South Ossetia.
Nikolai Makoyev, head of the North Ossetian Emergencies Ministry, told Itar-Tass news agency rescue workers had taken food, warm clothing and medicines to the people who had stayed.
"All the passengers of the vehicles which were snowbound for several days near Roksky Tunnel on the Transcaucasus highway were evacuated today to Vladikavkaz (North Ossetia's main city)," he said.
"They have been given the necessary assistance and fortunately there are no injured or sick people."
Makoyev said the situation around the four-km (2.5 mile) Roksky tunnel was still difficult because of continuing avalanches and landslides.
Russian news agencies had earlier this week put the number of people trapped in or near the tunnel at about 300.
Tass said on Monday that two women had given birth while trapped in the tunnel and one new-born child had died of the cold. Two other people were reported to have died in the area at the weekend.
In a separate operation, Tass said rescue workers had evacuated 300 people trapped by avalanches on a road running from the Georgian capital Tbilisi to Vladikavkaz.
It said they had been stranded between the Georgian towns of Mleta and Koba and were now staying in hotels and with local families.
